title: Prompt Engineering
summary: Design instructions that make LLM behavior more reliable and predictable, measured against a test set.
outcome: Write, test and version prompts systematically, and pick the best prompt by measurement rather than intuition.

project.title: Optimize a Real Prompt
deliverables: Pick one realistic task: classification, extraction, support answering or a domain assistant
Build a small test set and several competing prompt versions
Compare versions on correctness, instruction following, format adherence, consistency, token usage and latency/cost
Choose the final prompt from measured results, not intuition

modules.title: Anatomy of a prompt

topics.d: Instructions, context, input, constraints, examples and output requirements.
System, user and assistant roles and how instructions are prioritized.
Keep instructions clearly apart from user or external data.

modules.outcome: Structure any prompt into clear, separable parts.

modules.title: Zero-shot & few-shot prompting

topics.d: When a clear instruction suffices and when examples are required.
Examples that demonstrate behavior and format.
How quality, diversity and ordering change results.
In-context examples versus changing weights.

modules.outcome: Decide whether a task needs examples and write ones that help.

modules.title: Reasoning & decomposition

topics.d: Complex logic, planning, math, code and constraint-heavy tasks.
Extraction, classification and rewriting.
Breaking tasks into subproblems or steps.
Adapting prompts instead of blindly asking for step-by-step.

modules.outcome: Use reasoning prompts only where they pay off.

modules.title: System prompt design

topics.t: What belongs in a system prompt
topics.d: Purpose, behavior, constraints, boundaries and output expectations.
Separating application rules from per-task instructions.
What to do when information is missing or off-topic.
Simple guardrails without an endless rulebook.

modules.outcome: Write a system prompt that sets stable, predictable behavior for an app.

modules.title: Controlling output

topics.d: Style, length, headings, tables and JSON via instructions and examples.
When schema enforcement beats prompting.
Meaning in the prompt; format enforced in code.

modules.outcome: Get output in the format you need, enforcing it in code when it matters.

modules.title: Prompt reliability & debugging

topics.d: Ambiguity, conflicting constraints, bad examples, missing context or unclear output specs.
Normal cases, edge cases and known failures.

topics.t: Comparing versions on the same examples
topics.d: Judge versions across a fixed set, not single responses.
Systematic iteration to cut variance and regressions.

modules.outcome: Debug prompts with a test set instead of one-off tries.

modules.title: Prompt versioning, cost & caching

topics.d: Track which prompt and model produced each result.
Quality, latency, tokens and cost per variant.
Remove unneeded context and repeated instructions.
Stable prefixes that benefit from provider caching.

modules.outcome: Manage prompts as versioned, cost-aware artifacts.

modules.title: Prompt injection basics

topics.d: Treat external or user-controlled text as untrusted data.
Attempts to override instructions or extract hidden information.

topics.t: Wording is not a security boundary
topics.d: Code, not prompt wording, must govern permissions.
Advanced defenses are covered in AI Security.

modules.outcome: Recognize injection risk and keep security decisions out of the prompt.

modules.title: Capstone: Optimize a Real Prompt

topics.d: Classification, extraction, support answering or a domain assistant.

topics.t: A test set and competing prompt versions
topics.d: A small test set and several prompt versions.
Are outputs correct?
Do outputs follow the instructions?
Do outputs match the required format?
Are outputs stable across runs?
Tokens consumed per prompt.
Response time and cost per prompt.
Select the final prompt from the numbers.

modules.outcome: A prompt chosen and defended with measurements.
